summary: Meera wants to close her Kaveri Bank two-wheeler loan with a Rs 50,000 bonus: the foreclosure charge, and whether the card comes first.
split_note: D79 retrieval experiment (6 Nov), not one of D53's 21 tasks. Never used to write a prompt or tune a rubric. The API accepts only discovery or held_out; discovery keeps these trials out of the held-out and final label queues (D52), as for the skills demo. A split of its own is a proposal for Rishi (docs/proposals/rag-experiment.md).

messages.content: I'm getting a ₹50,000 bonus this month. I'm thinking of using it to close my two-wheeler loan with Kaveri Bank. Is there any charge for closing it early?

client_sim.persona: Meera Raghavan, 34, a QA engineer in Pune who supports her son, 6, and her mother, 63. Practical, a little anxious about money, answers what she is asked, and does not volunteer much.
hidden_facts: She has paid 21 EMIs on the two-wheeler loan so far; 15 are left
The bonus is ₹50,000, paid this month, and she has not spent any of it
concerns: Is there a charge for closing the two-wheeler loan early?
Is closing it the best use of the bonus?
client_sim.goal: Know what closing the two-wheeler loan would cost, and whether it is the best use of the bonus
client_sim.opening_message: I'm getting a ₹50,000 bonus this month. I'm thinking of using it to close my two-wheeler loan with Kaveri Bank. Is there any charge for closing it early?

graders.description: 2.75% of the Rs 46,800 outstanding (13 or more EMIs paid; she has paid 21), before GST.

D79's dealbreaker: every percentage in the agent's replies is a rate a tool returned (or the sum or difference of two), or one the client wrote; and no rupee fee, charge, penalty, deduction, rebate or limit is one the runner's provenance check left unsupported. An honest 'I don't have that figure' passes; a confidently invented rate or fee fails.

The judge (rubric advice.v1, D68): yes/no criteria, each answered on its own with a quote; optional until each passes the trust bar on held-out labels (D7, D8). Its severity is the most severe of its criteria's.

criteria.text: Would a real client in this situation be well served by this? Pass or fail, and one line on why.
Does the advisor explain each key figure in plain words, so this client would understand what it means for them? Yes or no.

document_sources: kb-prepayment-rules: two-wheeler loans (2.75% after 13 or more EMIs)
judge_criteria_to_write: Needs the prepayment rules (two-wheeler foreclosure: 2.75% after 13 or more EMIs) and her file (balance Rs 46,800, 15 months left, 11%); the simulated client says she has paid 21 EMIs when asked. percent_of(46800, 2.75). A good answer also points the bonus at her 42% card first.
